```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A is pure software: a vision model plus Shopify Admin API write-back. At least six live competitors ship this, so a solo operator with AI agents can plausibly build it. B needs physical fulfillment (customs, damaged goods, returns, address changes), which by its own brief is 'high-touch and low-margin' and poorly suited to a one-person AI-run company.",
    "A has a built-in, sourced distribution surface: the Shopify App Store, with a merchant-initiated install path. B's channels are generic Google Ads, sourced at $3.33–$6.29 CPC, and a Stripe marketplace listing gated by app review. Neither brief gives outreach evidence for B's buyer.",
    "Both markets are crowded, but A's competition is on differentiation and price inside a proven paying category. Paid tiers are sourced at $5–$129/mo. In B, the proposed core mechanic, a Stripe trigger that sends swag, is already a documented, marketed incumbent feature (SwagUp via Zapier, Sendoso via Tray.io/Pipedream). That leaves B without a stated wedge.",
    "A's unit economics are supported in the brief: 0% Shopify revenue share under $1M and cheap inference. B's economics are unresolved by its own open questions: all-in per-package cost at low volume, and $60–$220 kit costs against low-ACV signups.",
    "A has a clear, cheap path to a first paying customer within 90 days: ship a narrower or better listing at $12–30/mo. B's first customer requires either reselling on top of platforms that sell direct to the same buyer, or taking on vendor and inventory operations."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence rests mostly on vendor-produced marketing: a SwagUp customer story (BurnRate) and a Printfection case study (Endcrawl). The strongest third-party quote (Hampton) actually shows the need is already met by SwagUp plus Zapier, so it undercuts the case for a new entrant. The brief's 'real customs breakdown' claim has no source at all and counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A is favored mainly because B carries heavy operational burden and its core mechanic is already covered by incumbents, not because A has strong evidence of its own. A's case-for overstates its evidence: the 473-review incumbent is on a free plan, so it does not prove willingness to pay. Neither brief shows a new entrant winning a first paying customer. A's organic discovery against 100–470-review incumbents, and the risk of one-time catalog-cleanup churn, remain serious unknowns."
}
```
